sources.citation: Debbarma, Sheela. 2021. A comparative phonology of Kokborok dialects: an analytical study of literary Kokborok, Reang and Jamatia dialects. Ph.D. thesis, Dept. of English, Tripura University (guide Chaitali Gorai). 230 pp. Shodhganga hdl 10603/368085.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Reang word-stress rule. 4.2.5 Syllable structure in Reang (pp.139-51); 4.3.4 Tones in Reang Dialect (pp.166-67): three tones (rising, falling, level) distinguish homophones, e.g. /lai/ leaf (rising) / easy (falling) / to cross (level); sesquisyllabic prefixes retain tone. Only generic remark p.157 that 'stress or accent is also associated with tone.. in stress languages such as English'.

sources.note: Nothing. Ch.3 Phonology gives 6 vowels, 20 consonants and 'two tones i.e., high tone and low tone, which are contrastive to each other by the significant pitch differences' (3.4 Tones, pp.40-42); ch.5 syllable = nucleus + consonants + obligatory tone (p.56), light/heavy syllables (p.57). The words stress/accent do not occur in the scanned text.
